commit.message:
fix(og): rich link previews for Slack/Twitter (PR1: meta-refresh + tags) (#357)

* docs: spec for OG / Twitter Card link preview fixes

Documents the root cause of bare-link Slack unfurls (meta-refresh in
crawler HTML) and the planned two-PR rollout: urgent tag fix first,
then /embed/:id route and broader route coverage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: implementation plan for OG/Twitter Card link previews

13 tasks across 2 PRs. PR 1 fixes the meta-refresh bug + adds player
tags (the urgent Slack fix). PR 2 lands /embed/:id, route coverage,
and prod validation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(compute-js): extract ogTags helpers into their own module

Pull buildCrawlerHtml, escapeHtml, cleanText, truncateText out of
index.js into compute-js/src/ogTags.js so they can be unit-tested
in jsdom without Fastly bindings.

Key behaviour changes vs. inline version:
- Remove <meta http-equiv="refresh"> (fixes Slack unfurl bail-out)
- Add og:image:width / og:image:height (default 1200×630, overridable)
- Add optional video block for og:video:* and twitter:player:*
- Replace "Redirecting to..." body with a plain link

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compute-js): only emit og:image dims when both supplied; set defaults at call sites

Drop the hard-coded 1200×630 defaults from buildCrawlerHtml (now null/null)
and only emit og:image:width / og:image:height meta tags when both values are
truthy.  Pass explicit 1200×630 at the video (with videoMeta passthrough hook
for Task 3) and category call sites; leave handleProfileOgTags without dims so
avatars no longer claim to be 1200×630.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(compute-js): cover buildCrawlerHtml refresh removal + video block

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(compute-js): wire og:video + twitter:player into video page OG tags

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
feat: sim-suppression hooks for divine-brain virtual-persona PR runner (#351)

* feat(sim-suppression): hooks for divine-brain virtual-persona PR runner

Three small surface-level changes that let divine-brain's virtual-
persona PR runner (https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-brain) drive
divine.video against staging without contaminating production data:

1. **Firebase Analytics gate at initializeApp** (src/lib/analytics.ts).
   The existing GDPR consent gate is too late — Firebase auto-tracking
   via GTM fires `page_view` to G-FTDHC8JHYF before the consent
   listener gets a chance. Empirically verified: a 32s headless
   scroll session against divine.video produced 2 real GA4 sessions
   with `_fv=1` in the prod cohort. The new gate short-circuits
   `initializeAnalytics()` itself when `window.__DIVINE_ANALYTICS_DISABLED__`
   is set, so `initializeApp` is never called and no Firebase bootstrap
   happens.

2. **HubSpot script-tag guard** (index.html). The HubSpot tracker
   (`js-na2.hs-scripts.com/244466832.js`) loads independently of the
   Firebase consent listener and emits `track-na2.hubspot.com/__ptq.gif`
   page-view pixels. The static `<script src=...>` is replaced with a
   tiny inline guard that only injects the HubSpot script when the
   suppression flag is unset.

3. **Relay override hook** (src/lib/simRelay.ts + src/App.tsx). New
   `resolveRelayUrl()` / `resolveRelayUrls()` read
   `localStorage.DIVINE_RELAY_OVERRIDE` and use a wss:// override (with
   a defensive scheme check — non-wss values are ignored) when set.
   App.tsx's `defaultConfig` now wraps `PRIMARY_RELAY.url` and the
   bootstrap relay list in `resolveRelay*` so sim sessions route to
   `wss://relay.staging.divine.video` while production traffic
   (no flag set) gets the default unchanged.

Production behavior is unchanged: the suppression flag is never set
in production, so all three guards fall through to the original
behavior. Both flags are set by divine-brain's Stagehand
`page.addInitScript` BEFORE document parse, so the guards see them.

Tests:
  src/lib/simRelay.test.ts            — 7 specs (override
                                          accept/reject, scheme guard,
                                          empty value, array variant,
                                          non-prod entries preserved)
  src/lib/analytics-suppression.test.ts — 2 specs (initializeAnalytics
                                          early-return, trackEvent
                                          no-op under suppression)

Empirical motivation + cross-references:
  divine-brain commit b700ba0 — first real-world smoke run that
  surfaced these three gaps:
  https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-brain/blob/main/docs/notes/2026-05-08-first-real-persona-run.md

Re-running the smoke after this PR ships should produce
`prod_relay_touched: false`, `analytics_events_emitted: 0`, exit 0.

* fix: move HubSpot guard out of inline script

revert: undo three-state age gate (#348) (#354)

* Revert "fix(player): use NIP-98 for age-gated viewer auth (#348)"

This reverts commit 7c874a4bd3c1526b5d92d3984c49b972f2bfd4dc.

* fix: preserve NIP-98 viewer auth from #348

Keep the BUD-01 → NIP-98 fix for MP4 direct fetches. Blossom's viewer
auth rejects BUD-01 get events; NIP-98 (kind 27235) works correctly.
This was the non-regressing part of #348.

* test: revert incidental cleanups from age-gate revert

Two small cleanups to keep this PR a tight scoped revert:

- funnelcakeTransform.test.ts: restore U+2019 (right single quote) in
  "world's"; the PR accidentally introduced U+2018 (left single quote /
  high-reversed-9), looks like editor smart-quote drift.
- VideoCard.test.tsx: restore the VideoPlayer mock's hlsUrl prop and
  data-hls-url attribute. Removing it lost test surface for asserting
  what HLS URL VideoCard passes through, and isn't related to the
  age-gate revert.

commit.message:
feat: linkify bare nostr identifiers in note content (#355)

NoteContent and InlineNostrText only matched the NIP-21 prefixed form
(nostr:npub1...). User-typed video descriptions and bios commonly use
the bare form (npub1..., note1..., etc.) which rendered as plain text.

- Make `nostr:` prefix optional via `(?:nostr:)?` in both regexes.
- Add `\b` word boundaries to prevent mid-word false matches like
  `xxxnpub1...yyy`.
- Add `naddr1` to NoteContent (was missing — kind 30000+ addressable
  refs weren't linkified).
- Add tests covering bare + prefixed forms for every supported
  identifier type, plus regression coverage for URLs and hashtags.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(player): use NIP-98 for age-gated viewer auth (#348)

* fix: preserve unknown age-gate state in Funnelcake transform

* fix: enrich classics feed with moderation age-gate metadata

* fix: block protected subtitles and prefetch before verification

* fix: show age gate for protected media with unknown status

* fix: CI

* fix(player): add auth headers for protected media with unknown age status

VideoPlayer gated auth header injection on `videoData?.ageRestricted`
(truthy check). Classic vines with unknown moderation status have
ageRestricted=undefined, so auth was never added after age verification
even though Blossom requires it. Uses `!== false` + URL check to match
the pattern in #279.

* fix(player): use NIP-98 for viewer auth instead of BUD-01

Blossom's media_viewer_context validates BUD-01 events with
AuthAction::List, rejecting the ['t', 'get'] events the player
sends. NIP-98 (kind 27235) validates correctly for all viewer
endpoints. The HLS auth loader already uses NIP-98; this aligns
the MP4 direct-fetch path to match.

* test(player): update auth header test to expect NIP-98 (no sha256)

Blossom's viewer auth rejects BUD-01 get events, so the player now
uses NIP-98 for all viewer requests. Update the test to match.

* fix(player): only auth poster for explicitly age-restricted videos

The !== false pattern on poster auth was too aggressive — it tried
to authenticate posters for all videos with unknown moderation
status, breaking poster display when the user hasn't verified yet.
Poster auth should only trigger for explicitly restricted content.
The preflight HEAD check handles discovery for unknown status.

* test(player): cover ageRestricted undefined/false auth paths, drop stale dep

Add test cases for the two untested branches: ageRestricted===undefined
triggers auth (unknown moderation status treated as potentially restricted),
ageRestricted===false skips auth entirely. Remove videoData?.sha256 from
the effect dependency array since the MP4 fetch no longer uses it.

* chore: document poster and card age-gate design decisions

Explain why poster auth uses truthy-only (not !== false) and why
VideoCard gates on explicit true only. Both are intentional: the
preflight HEAD check handles unknown-status discovery at playback
time, avoiding false positives in the card grid and poster loading.

* fix(auth): propagate three-state ageRestricted through thumbnail auth

VideoGrid and ThumbnailPlayer coerced undefined to false via !!, causing
verified users to get 401s on thumbnails for unknown-status protected
media. Pass ageRestricted through unchanged and treat undefined as
"maybe restricted" in useAuthenticatedMediaUrl (ageRestricted !== false).

VideoPlayer poster intentionally keeps !! (comment explains why).

Regression tests: verified user gets auth on unknown-status, auth skipped
on explicitly safe media.

---------

Co-authored-by: Dmitriy E <dsanichweb@gmail.com>

commit.message:
feat(i18n): add Filipino (fil) locale for PH growth (#349)

* feat(i18n): add Filipino (fil) locale for PH growth

Adds Filipino as a supported locale (code `fil`, label "Filipino")
with brand-voice translations across all 11 namespaces.

- `tl`, `tl-PH`, and `fil-PH` browser locales all alias to `fil`
  so users on older or newer OS settings get matched.
- Voice tuned for PH internet-native users: Taglish where natural
  ("Loops ng mga sinusundan mo.", "Tara, sumama sa community"),
  English kept for nav/category labels (matches TikTok/IG/FB-PH
  convention), formal register only on legal/policy section
  titles where it belongs.
- Existing locale-parity test covers key completeness; alias
  resolution test added in config.test.ts.

A native PH reviewer should sanity-check `common.json` brand
strings before this ships ("Uwi na tayo.", "Sagot ka namin.",
the NIP-44 signer fallback paragraph).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(i18n): full Filipino translation pass + lift hardcoded strings into i18n

Two issues surfaced when QAing the Filipino locale on a deploy preview:
many UI strings still rendered in English even with Filipino selected.

Cause #1: my initial Taglish strategy left nav/categories/discovery labels
in English (Music/Sports/Discover/Categories/Hot/Tags etc.). Other locales
follow a full-translation pattern (Spanish: Inicio/Descubrir/Categorias/
Musica), so Filipino now matches: Tahanan/Tuklasin/Mga Kategorya/Musika/
Sayaw/Komedya/Paglalakbay/Pamilya/Pagkain/Teknolohiya/etc. Sports, Fashion,
and Profile/Analytics stay as loanwords where Tagalog has no commonly-used
native term.

Cause #2: four prominent strings were hardcoded in components and never
went through i18n at all. Lifted them into the catalog and wired t():
- "Log in" (LoginArea) → auth.logIn
- "Classic Viners" (ClassicVinersRow header) → discovery.classicViners
- "Play all" (VideoFeed + SearchPage compilation buttons) → common.playAll
- "Archived" + tooltip (VineBadge) → vineBadge.archived / vineBadge.tooltip

New keys added to all 16 locales (English placeholders for the 14 non-fil
non-en locales — they can be properly translated in follow-up PRs).

Also addressed PR review feedback on the alias logic:
- Removed redundant `fil: 'fil'` entry from LOCALE_ALIASES (never reached
  because SUPPORTED_LOCALES includes 'fil' and is checked first).
- Split the alias test into two: one for legacy `tl`/`tl-PH` aliases
  (LOCALE_ALIASES path), one for `fil-PH` regional variants
  (standard split-on-dash fallback). Was misleading to lump them together.

Test setup: VideoFeed/SearchPage/LoginArea tests now init i18n and stub
localStorage in beforeEach (matching the AppSidebar.test.tsx pattern).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(i18n): wire VideoCard through useTranslation (~30 strings)

Lifts every user-facing string in VideoCard into the i18n catalog
under the new `videoCard` namespace in common.json:

- 12 aria-labels (subtitles, mute, fullscreen, like/unlike, repost,
  view-likes/reposts, comment, share, download, lists, more options)
- 7 toast title/description pairs (mute success/fail, pin/unpin
  success/fail, download error/start)
- 8 dropdown menu items (pin/unpin, delete, report video/user, send
  via DM, view source, mute user)
- Repost-attribution strings with i18n plural support
  (repostedBySingle / repostedByMultiple_one / _other)
- Failed-load + retry copy, age-gate action labels, loading-profile
  fallback, view-source dialog title

Filipino translations follow the brand-aligned full-translation
pattern (e.g., "I-mute si {name}", "Burahin ang video", "Wala na
sa feed mo si {name}.").

The 14 non-en/non-fil locales got English placeholders for now —
quality translations should follow in per-locale review PRs.

Test setup: VideoCard.test.tsx now inits i18n + stubs localStorage
in beforeEach (matching the LoginArea/VideoFeed/SearchPage pattern
established earlier in this branch).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(i18n): wire 13 dialog/profile components (~272 strings) via parallel agents

Second pass of i18n rollout: dispatched 5 parallel subagents to wire
high-impact dialog and profile surfaces. Each agent edited its
component(s) directly and emitted a JSON patch to /tmp/i18n-patches/;
patches were aggregated and merged into all 16 locales centrally to
avoid race conditions on common.json.

Components wired (with new namespace per component):
- addToListDialog (27 keys)
- createListDialog (31 keys)
- editListDialog (29 keys)
- zapDialog (20 keys)
- walletModal (31 keys)
- profileHeader (26 keys)
- loginDialog (41 keys)
- accountSwitcher (7 keys)
- reportContentDialog (26 keys)
- deleteVideoDialog (10 keys)
- viewSourceDialog (13 keys)
- ageVerificationOverlay (8 keys)
- badgeDetailModal (4 keys)

Total: 273 keys × 16 locales.

Filipino translations follow the established pattern (Spanish-style
full translation, Tagalog `I-` prefix on English verbs where natural,
brand-voice casual-direct tone). The 14 non-en/non-fil locales got
English placeholder values for the new keys — translation-quality
follow-up needed per locale.

Test setup: 5 component test files that touched the new t() calls
got the standard localStorage stub + initializeI18n boilerplate added
to beforeEach.

Verification:
- 727/727 vitest tests pass
- tsc --noEmit clean

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(i18n): wire 22 more components/pages (~418 strings) via parallel agents

Batch 2 of i18n rollout. Five parallel subagents wired:
- Settings: ModerationSettingsPage, LinkedAccountsSettingsPage, LinkedAccounts (100 keys)
- Analytics: AnalyticsPage, LeaderboardPage, DebugVideoPage (57 keys)
- Forms: EditProfileForm, VideoMetadataForm, UploadPage (55 keys)
- Content pages: VideoPage, ProfilePage, CategoryPage, HashtagPage,
  ListDetailPage, ConversationPage (160 keys, with plural forms)
- Feed components: VideoCommentsModal, VideoPlayer, ThumbnailPlayer,

commit.message:
fix(video): show event description on video page, not title-as-content (#343)

The Funnelcake transform was mapping `raw.title` into `ParsedVideoData.content`
("Funnelcake uses title field for content"). VideoCard guards against
duplicating the title by rendering content only when it differs from the
title, so the actual Nostr `content` field — the user-authored description —
never made it to the page.

Map `raw.content` through instead. The single-video endpoint
(`/api/videos/{id}`) already populates `raw.content` from `event.content`
in `fetchVideoById`. List endpoints that omit content fall through to an
empty string, which the existing VideoCard guard already handles.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
